Most “vanilla” foods are colored to match the public idea of vanilla: pale cream or white, like vanilla ice cream or milk.

Vanilla beans themselves are dark brown-black, but the flavor compounds are extracted from the beans into a liquid. In small amounts, that extract usually doesn’t darken a whole batch much—especially in a white base like milk, cream, frosting, or cake batter. Manufacturers may also filter the extract or use clear/artificial vanillin.

When you use real vanilla bean or vanilla bean paste, you often *do* see the tiny black specks. Those specks are mostly used as a visual signal that real vanilla was used.
